title: OCP: Open/Closed
points: Open for extension, closed for modification.
Add new behaviour by adding new code (a new class), not editing tested code.
trade: Usually achieved with polymorphism (Strategy). Don't pre-abstract before you see a second variant (YAGNI).
test: What smell in code tells you OCP is being violated?
answer: A growing if/else or switch on a type that you must edit for every new variant.

questions.question: discount(Customer c) has an if/else for each customer type, and you edit it for every new type. What is the best refactor?
options: A DiscountPolicy interface with one class per type
Move the logic into the Customer constructor
questions.explanation: OCP: new type means a new class implementing DiscountPolicy, with existing code untouched.
